key_insight: Mesoscale neural operators learn nonlocal constitutive laws from molecular dynamics data while preserving key fracture energetics across scales.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables continuum fracture simulations on much larger domains and coarser grids than atomistic simulations can practically handle.
method: Learn a nonlocal kernel and nonlinear constitutive relation from MD loading and displacement data.
Normalize the kernel to preserve strain energy density under horizon rescaling.
Rescale critical bond stretch to maintain consistent energy release rates across scales.
evidence_signal: Synthetic tests supported model recovery; an MD-based test matched fracture energetics within 3%, out-of-distribution tension tests predicted peak forces within 6%, and a plate demonstration reproduced branching fracture over 4000× the training-specimen area.
watch_item: The reported tests do not establish transferability to other materials or loading regimes without additional validation.
paper_title: Mesoscale Neural Operators: Learning Nonlinear Constitutive Laws from Molecular Dynamics for Scalable Fracture Predictions
